text:
kelly: heads up — onboarding for tenant acme-inc is failing during SCIM provisioning and we lost a few SAML audit events. Seeing a 409 from SCIM and no corresponding user-create entries in the audit index. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: which 409? conflict on externalId or an internal dup? paste the logs pls.

kelly: here's the SCIM error from the provisioning service: `HTTP 409 Conflict {\"detail\": \"User with externalId already exists\"}` but the idp UI shows the user wasn't fully created. also audit-index shows a gap: user.create event missing for that timeframe (2026-03-18T15:12Z).

anika: odd — could be we wrote the entry but audit pipeline failed to decrypt metadata before indexing. any KMS errors in the provisioning logs?

kelly: checking... paste of provisioning service log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T15:11:58Z INFO provisioning: start create user externalId=acme-ops-4421
2026-03-18T15:12:00Z ERROR provisioning.kms: failed to decrypt envelope: AccessDenied
2026-03-18T15:12:00Z ERROR provisioning: create aborted due to kms decrypt failure
2026-03-18T15:12:00Z WARN provisioning: attempting retry x1
2026-03-18T15:12:02Z ERROR scim: http 409 conflict from idp (duplicate extId)
```

sam: there — KMS decrypt failed, provisioning aborted, but the idp reported duplicate extId (race). So SCIM client got a 409 while our create was partially retried. The audit entry wasn't emitted because the create flow aborted before publishing. KMS AccessDenied is the root.

jonah: AccessDenied from KMS often points to a key policy or role ARN change. Did acme-inc land in a cross-account onboarding flow recently? Any role changes in the last 24h?

kelly: we rotated the provisioning instance role last night (to tighten permissions). I assumed it had kms:Decrypt on the alias but maybe not on the key.

anika: important distinction — alias resource policy vs CMK key policy. If role is only allowed on alias, that doesn't guarantee Decrypt unless key policy allows that principal. check the key policy for `alias/redwood/provisioning-acme` and the grant table.

sam: quick check commands that helped me before:
```
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01 --policy
aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-ef01
aws sts get-caller-identity --output json
```
Run as the service principal from the provisioning instance. If sts shows the new role, and list-grants is empty or missing a grant for that role, that's likely it.

jonah: also check CloudTrail for `KMS:Decrypt` events around 15:12. It should show who attempted and the error code.

kelly: ran sts and list-grants as the service role — list-grants shows a grant but for a different principal (old role ARN). we rotated role, didn't create a new grant. that explains it.

anika: yeah. two safe remediation options: 1) add the new role to the CMK key policy (or recreate a grant for it), or 2) roll the provisioning role back to the previous ARN while we create a proper grant. Option 1 preferred long-term.

sam: +1 for grant creation so we avoid policy churn. note that grants expire if created with TTL. also confirm that the grant allows Decrypt and `kms:GenerateDataKey` if envelope encryption is used.

kelly: created a grant with `Operations: [\"Decrypt\",\"GenerateDataKey\"]` for the new role and re-ran the onboarding. SCIM now returns 201 for that user but audit still missing for several earlier attempts — indexer didn't get the failed events. any way to reconcile?

jonah: we should replay the failed provisioning events from the provisioning service dead-letter queue (DLQ) or logs and re-emit audit.create for any successfully created users that lack an audit row. do we have DLQ enabled for that consumer?

kelly: provisioning DLQ has entries for the 15:12 batch. will replay to audit topic. planning to run a targeted replay for acme-inc users between 15:10-15:20.

anika: one more SAML side note — I noticed the SAML assertion from acme-idp used NameIDFormat=transient during the race. Our onboarding expects persistent NameID for linking to extId. If the IDP sometimes sends transient it can mis-link and produce duplicate extId attempts. worth flagging with the customer.

kelly: good catch. acme's SAML config has both persistent and transient as accepted formats. I'll ask them to pin to persistent for user provisioning flows.

sam: for post-mortem record: root cause = provisioning role rotation without matching KMS grant; secondary amplifying factor = IDP sending transient NameID causing a race/duplicate extId report. Remediation: created grant, replayed DLQ, asked customer to pin NameIDFormat, added an onboarding check that fails loudly if NameIDFormat != persistent.

jonah: add to runbook: when rotating provisioning role, update CMK grants (or use IAM principal-based key policy) and verify via `aws kms decrypt` smoke test. Also add a monitoring alert for `KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied` spikes in the provisioning service.

kelly: creating a small RFC to update onboarding docs and we'll run the replay now. will post status when DLQ replay completes.

infra-bot: DLQ replay job started for provisioning-topic (job id rpr-20260318-01).

kelly: DLQ replay complete — audit rows for acme users restored, no further 409s in last 30m. closing for now. thanks all :tada:
